My friend @Pinyaka and I have made a pact to do a 30 day sit and keep up with each other. I update here and Pinyaka does so in the comment below. Anyone wanting to join us may post a comment as well and update it as much and as less as they wish, but hopefully daily. Even a "Did" or "Didn't" will suffice as a day's entry. Cheers!

So here's how each day so far has gone:

Day 1/30:

Back from a late night out with friends. Need to wake up to cycle ~8 next morning. set a timer for 24 minutes. A bit more than I should've done. Focused attention on my breathing, then the point on my nostrils where I felt my inhalations and exhalations meet. I relaxed everything that was around that point. My thoughts, my sensations, my feelings, my desires. When I felt myself straining, I told myself this was a vacation from everything. I didn't need to be anything or think anything. I could simply observe. My attention drifted a lot. To events that happened today, things I want to do, the pain in my back keeping myselff straight. When I realised that I was, I relaxed my thinking around my goal. I visualised the point between my nostril as the point around which everything blurred. Pain blurred around it. Noise blurred around it. Thoughts dissolved into wisps around it. I wasn't entirely successful, but it was a session.

I ended my practice with several minutes of loving-kindness meditation. I wished, one by one, my loved friends and family well, that they'd find happiness and peace. I moved to people I barely knew, people I didn't like, people that were sufferring, and most importantly, me. I have a hard time loving myself, so I always leave it for the end. I told myself that my unpredictable, unruly imp-mind was beloved to me, and I hoped that it would find peace and happiness, and that I would receive every hurtful thought with equanimity and return it with love.

Going to sleep at 2:17.

Day 2/30:

Started at 12:30 am. 24 minutes. Fell asleep a lot. Amusing session. But glad to report no more back pain! Back workout with a steel band earlier in the day helped. Forgot to do loving-kindness, though.

Day 3/30:

Didn't formally meditate. But did so for a few minutes when I was waiting for someone and as I was going to sleep.

Day 4/30:

Did 15 minutes before sleeping. There was lots of distracting music, but I returned to my breathing every time I noticed myself veering off course and sat through the whole thing. Did an extended loving-kindness session, I've grown to like them very much.

Soon after in bed, I mediated to sleep as I was too excited and couldn't sleep. It was effective.

Day 5/30:

Woke up at 5 to go swimming with a friend. Felt tired, so I put a 15 minute timer on to meditate, but was interrupted by her call in the middle. Didn't continue.

Day 6/30:

Didn't meditate. Felt the urge to at several points of time in the day. I briefly closed my eyes and focused on my breath until a video I was watching loaded, but that was barely 15 seconds. I doubt it counts.

23rd May, Day 7/30:

Great session. 20 minutes. Started at 2 am (I consider that the today's night), need to wake up to go to the dog park next morning.

Very distracted session, but I could really sense my mind clearing up as the time ticked on. I think 20 minutes must be where i start to see results, because I've noticed this in the past. Cannot wait for tomorrow's session!

On a related note, I bought several books today, amongst them a book on meditation, one on Buddhism and a few on Philosophy. I'm already halfway through one of them; I hope to learn a lot.

Day 8/30:

I closed my eyes and meditated while I waited for my girlfriend to come out from where she lives. A good 10 minutes.

Later that night, I convinced my friend to try meditating with me. We did a ten-minute session while I gave instructions. We also did some loving-kindness. All in all, a good day.

Day 9/30:

Have to wake up for swimming tomorrow. I sat for 24 minutes, in the first few of which I remembered to eat my medicine, so I got up and quickly sat back down without disturbing the timer.

I had an utterly chaotic session. My awareness simply wouldn't stay put, owing to some exciting plans I had made just prior to sitting. But I smiled and kept at it in my own patient way, finally managing to sustain awareness for minutes on end at the end. I enjoyed this today's session. I must go to sleep now.

Days 10-15:

Went through an emotionally troubled period. Didn't meditate.

Day 16/30:

I meditated for 10 minutes early in the morning. Great way to kick off the second half of my 30 day sit! The middle is always the most difficult part. I'm thinking of starting a 30daysit sub so more people can participate!

Edit: Back from my shower, but still feel really excited. Don't want to sleep. Scared of trying to do wholesome things and failing.

Edit 2: My sister woke up, needing me to sleep in her room and take care of our dogs and puppies while she does her online music lessons. This turned out to be a boon in disguise. Her room was dark, making it uncomfortable to use the computer. I used this as an opportunity and set a timer for 17 minutes.

I must say, this was one of the easiest and most pleasant sessions I've ever done. Sitting was physically easy, and mentally, too, I didn't struggle one bit. This time I took special care not to rush and push myself onto my object of concentration. Instead, every time I got distracted, I observed the distraction until it melted away by itself and left me to my breathing. And in the process of going away, the thoughts left me with small insights about the nature of my mind. I found a lot of them leading me to the same conclusion, which was surprising. It appears that I desperately wanted people to praise me, and that this is the motivation behind most of my thoughts and actions. A mighty useful thing to know about oneself, wouldn't you say? I realize now that one needn't wait for impeccable concentration to start to observe and receive insights into their being. It can integrated into your practice right from the beginning. All in all, my attention must have been on the object only about 40% of the time, but the time spent away from it left me with a deep sense of understanding and to a smaller extent peace, with the kind of person I was. Incidentally, I'd noticed several times in the beginning that the bell hadn't rung, but I carried on anyway. When I decided I was done and opened my eyes, I found that my 17-minute timer had mysteriously stopped at 16:13 and I'd meditated for a whopping 40 minutes. A pleasing result.

Day 17/30:

Don't remember whether or not I meditated. Leaning towards yes.

Day 18/30:

Went to Mysore for the weekend, met very interesting people. Forgot to meditate during the day. Couldn't do it before sleeping because I had to wake up for hiking very early the next morning.

Day 19/30:

Couchsurfed at my friends' place, meditated for 20 minutes before sleeping.

Day 20/30:

I travelled by train for about 3 hours today, and meditated for the most of it. It was difficult, as I kept fantasizing about plans I'd made and falling asleep alternatively (it was early in the morning).

I also did around 20 minutes at night.

Day 21/30:

Meditated for 24 minutes before sleeping.

Day 21/30 to 30/30:

Meditated, but only while going to sleep. These ten days of mine mirrored /u/Pinyaka's. Got derailed. No worries, time to start again. :)
Let's try this again - let's do a 30 day sit

Day 1

Today I tried sitting at the end of the day before going through my nightly "getting ready for bed routing." I set a timer for 15 minutes but acknowledged that I probably wouldn't make it through the full 15 minutes as I was using the time while my wife was showering/getting ready for bed. I sat on my couch and ran through my body relaxing tension as I found it and then brought my attention back to the sensation of breathing. I counted up to ten breaths and then started over. My attention mostly drifted to planning for work tomorrow and chores that I wasn't able to finish today. I ended up sitting for less than 10 minutes which is better than nothing.

Day 2

Sat again at the end of the day before the nightly preparation for bed, this time for right at 10 minutes. After breathing out tension, I tried to keep my focus on the feeling of air flowing in through my nostrils but found myself continually distracted by planning for the future (work tomorrow, trip this weekend, work that needs to be done on the house). I count my breaths in sets of 10 and I don't think I spent more than 10 consecutive breaths on any one distraction, but I also don't think I got a full 10 breaths without a distraction.

Day 3

Quick sit tonight. Right before the session I got into an argument with my wife and so bits of that kept floating back through my head. There wasn't much chance that the session was going to go well, so I mostly just wanted to make sure that I just sat for a few minutes to continue the habit of taking some time to literally go through the motions.

Day 4

I started sitting tonight after a mini-marathon of Cities: Skylines and so I started with some distractions in the form of afterimages from the video game and then even more planning type thoughts. I really only sat through a few minutes before the urge to figure out how to plan traffic patterns overpowered me and I stopped.

Day 5

Did not meditate today. I was rushing around to get ready for a trip this weekend and I didn't think about it until too late.

I'm adding the stuff from here through Day 10 on day 10, so these are just recollections

Day 6 5/23

Spent most of the day travelling so I didn't get a formal meditation in. I flew a lot and I experience moderate anxiety during takeoff, landing and periods with more turbulence than usual. As is my custom, during these periods I practice a kind of light meditation where I put away books, videos, music, etc. and focus on the physical sensations surrounding these disturbances. Normally my anxiety subsides and today was no exception. I got to practice during two takeoff/landing periods and also for about 10 minutes due to consecutive turbulence.

Day 7 5/24

I spent the day visiting friends and doing touristy stuff in New York City, somewhere I've not really been before. Again, I didn't get in a formal meditation, but I have tendonitis in my left knee and after a whirlwind tour of the Met and an hour or so in the Natural History Museum, I had to sit down. Not wanting to slow down my friends who were also there and not having enough charge on my phone to play with it, I went outside and sat on a bench. My mind kept failing to grasp the scale of the city, so I spent some time looking out over East Dr. and letting the sensations of the city wash over me.

Day 8 5/25

Flew back home today. No practice other than the normal periods of sensory focus during takeoffs and landings. There was no turbulence to speak of.

Day 9 5/26

Did not meditate.

Day 10

Today I decided to do my practice in the morning after breakfast. I sat for 10 minutes and focused on my breathing. I've got some issues surrounding a project that I'm working on for work and my mind kept fluctuating between fixating on that and trying to rephrase the way I thought about in terms of a blog post I read this morning. I don't know how effective the meditation was, but not berating myself about what I "should" be doing today was accompanied by a day of unusual productivity for me.

Day 11

Since yesterday went so well, I decided to do my sitting in the morning after breakfast again. Today I set a timer and actually sat for 15 minutes. My mind kept racing to plan for the day: when should I go into work? How will I respond to an email? Don't forget to put some gum in your bag. Junk like that. I don't think that I ever got more than three or four consecutive breaths that I paid attention to. Still, it's a session and I feel good about having done it before starting my day and also for going longer than I normally would have.

Day 12

Did another 15 minute session, this time in the evening after some physical therapy exercises. Mostly it went okay, but I did have a few minutes in the middle where I got distracted thinking about criticism an audiobook that I'm listening to. Oddly, the criticism actually led me back to thinking about the importance of meditation and I was able to get on with the rest of the session.

Day 13-28

No practice during this period. I had several things during the last two weeks that caused a lot of anxiety. Meditation probably would have been helpful during this period, but mostly I found that when I wasn't dealing directly with the problems I was having (personal and professional) I didn't want to think about them, so I sought out a lot of distractions.

Day 29

After the two-week hiatus, I did a 15 minute sit today. I haven't been sleeping well and I caught myself nodding off two or three times and then finally fell asleep sitting up. I sort of reverse drooled and woke up with a coughing fit.
